# Inner normalizer covariance and outer conditional laws

## Result and scope

**(P, as an implication from the explicit C06/C08 input inequalities.)** For any fixed-history conditional law satisfying (OH.3)–(OH.6), the covariance term generated by differentiating its inner normalizer is uniformly exponentially localized when the stated spatial majorants hold. More sharply, its quadratic form is bounded above by the exact principal Gaussian Schur contribution plus a quantity of order `P_k^{-2}`. The proof uses the complete interacting conditional law on its literal convex product cutoff. It makes no Gaussian replacement and retains the normalizer derivative. This note does not independently verify the open C05 actual-history estimate that is used upstream to supply those inequalities uniformly on every required Wilson history; the Schur implication remains rigorous independently of that application question.

**(C.)** This gives a concrete sufficient test for coercivity of the same-current outer marginal: after extracting the principal exterior quadratic, one must control an explicitly identified outer curvature defect and the actual outer support. On a fixed convex outer domain satisfying that test, the outer covariance application follows.

**(O.)** The full retained-history law has not passed that test. Retained-only selectors, geometry changes, the relocation Jacobian and history factors remain in its outer density; they did not disappear when the inner law was normalized. C08 consequently does not establish H04/H05, the amended all-history M04/M07 estimate, or the ER.7 physically normalized hierarchy bound.

For M04, the original full-footprint norm has a first-step obstruction from the geometry of the integration support. A local-mask amendment preserves the physical law, but its arbitrary-depth common-family and current bounds remain unproved. This is an interface correction, not a counterexample to Yang–Mills existence.

## 1. The exact current variables and outer factor

Use the notation of [Response to exterior current coordinates](../physical_scale/retained_current_response.md), RC.1–RC.4 and RC.23–RC.24. At one fixed admitted history, let `z` be the integrated free current coordinates `I` and let `y` be the retained free coordinates `O` of the **same** current chart. In the source convention

\[
 O=(\Omega_{k+1}\cap\Lambda_{k+1}^{c})^{(k)*}.
 \tag{OH.1}
\]

The coarse datum, earlier raw fields, coupling and geometry are fixed. These variations are not arbitrary older retained-coordinate or history variations. The full constrained principal matrix was formed before conditioning:

\[
 \mathcal K=
 \begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ B^T&D_0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad A=K_{II},\quad B=K_{IO},\quad D_0=K_{OO}.
 \tag{OH.2}
\]

The source identities `QC=0`, `Qh=I` and `D(q)=N(q-hD(q))` imply that changing `y` within this chart keeps the prescribed coarse field and `mathcal K` fixed. The exact conditional law is

\[
 \nu_y(dz)=Z(y)^{-1}\mathbf1_{D_I}(z)e^{H(z,y)}\,dz,
 \qquad
 H(z,y)=-\tfrac12z^TAz-z^TBy+W(z,y),
 \tag{OH.3}
\]

where `D_I` is C07's literal fixed product of symmetric convex free-bond balls. All terms with nonzero `z`-gradient occur in `W` in their actual source allocation. Write the continuous part of the actual outer density, on a fixed active stratum, as

\[
 \pi(dy)\propto
 \mathbf1_{D_O}(y)\,q(y)e^{-\frac12y^TD_0y}Z(y)\,dy.
 \tag{OH.4}
\]

Here `q` means every remaining outer factor after the displayed principal exterior quadratic has been extracted. The indicator notation does not assert that `D_O` is convex, a product, or even described by one smooth boundary. Factors depending only on `y` include the applicable retained selectors, exterior coarea/measure factors, relocation Jacobian and inherited normalization/history factors. They canceled from (OH.3), but they remain in (OH.4). Other continuous or discrete retained data may still lie outside this chart altogether.

The distinction is already explicit in RC.3–RC.4: the mixed current estimate does not assert a full exterior-law Hessian. The present note makes the normalizer part of that exterior Hessian quantitative.

## 2. The complete inner and mixed inequalities used as inputs

The input inequalities appearing in the conditional-law C06/C08 conditional theorem are, at a fixed smaller spatial rate,

\[
 A\succeq\lambda_0I,\qquad
 \|W_{zz}(z,y)\|_{2\to2}\le\varepsilon_k,
 \qquad
 \|W_{zy}(z,y)\|_{2\to2}\le\varepsilon_k,
 \qquad \varepsilon_k=C_*P_k^{-2}.
 \tag{OH.5}
\]

Increase `C_*` to cover both sectors. For the implication proved here, require these bounds uniformly in the chosen real inner and same-current exterior chart, with fixed entrywise matrices having bounded weighted rows and columns. They must not be obtained by interchanging a supremum and a row sum. Their application to all original histories is not a new conclusion of this note. For sufficiently weak coupling, `epsilon_k < lambda_0/2`. Set

\[
 H_I(z,y)=A-W_{zz}(z,y)\succeq(\lambda_0-\varepsilon_k)I.
 \tag{OH.6}
\]

The exact source precision has uniform exponentially summable rows, so `kappa = ||B||_{2->2}` is bounded independently of volume and history. Block dimensions are fixed by the gauge group and free-coordinate convention.

The same-current score is

\[
 S(z,y)=\nabla_yH(z,y)=-B^Tz+\nabla_yW(z,y),
 \qquad \widehat S=S-\nu_yS,
 \tag{OH.7}
\]

and

\[
 D_{y_a}\nu_y=\widehat S_a\nu_y.
 \tag{OH.8}
\]

The denominator derivative in (OH.8) is essential. RC.7–RC.9 and C8Y.3–C8Y.5 already prove the corresponding first normalized response and its uniform centered `L^p` bound.

## 3. A matrix Brascamp–Lieb consequence on the literal cutoff

### Lemma OH.1 — the actual inner variance form

For every real scalar `f` in the indicated Sobolev domain,

\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\nu_y}(f)
 \le
 \nu_y\!\left[(\nabla_zf)^T H_I^{-1}(\nabla_zf)\right].
 \tag{OH.9}
\]

**Proof.** First replace each literal norm ball by an increasing smooth convex inner approximation, as in C8A.12–C8A.14. On its product, the differentiated scalar Neumann form for a vector field `u` is the sum of the nonnegative kinetic term, the multiplication term `u^TH_Iu`, and the nonnegative boundary second-fundamental-form term. Let its operator be `mathscr A`. The scalar covariance representation gives

\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\nu_y}(f)
 =\langle\nabla f,\mathscr A^{-1}\nabla f\rangle.
\]

Use the variational expression for the inverse quadratic form. Since the form of `mathscr A` is at least the multiplication form of `H_I`,

\[
 \begin{split}
 \langle v,\mathscr A^{-1}v\rangle
 &=\sup_{u\in\mathcal D(\mathfrak a)}
       \{2\langle v,u\rangle-\mathfrak a(u,u)\}\\
 &\le\sup_{u\in L^2}
       \{2\langle v,u\rangle-\nu_y[u^TH_Iu]\}
 =\nu_y[v^TH_I^{-1}v].
 \end{split}
\]

The last equality is pointwise completion of the square. Taking `v=gradient f` proves (OH.9) on each approximation. The coefficients and the positive lower bound are continuous on the fixed admitted compact chart. Scalar density convergence and Sobolev approximation therefore pass the inequality to the literal product, exactly as in the existing C08 scalar argument. This proves the asserted scalar inequality without asserting convergence of an arbitrary-vector boundary realization. ∎

### Theorem OH.2 — a sharp one-sided normalizer covariance bound

Let

\[
 C_\nu(y)=\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu_y}(S,S).
\]

Then, for `0 <= epsilon_k < lambda_0`,

\[
 0\preceq C_\nu(y)
 \preceq B^TA^{-1}B+\delta_k I,
 \tag{OH.10}
\]

where the explicit uniform error is

\[
 \delta_k=
 \frac{\kappa^2\varepsilon_k}{\lambda_0(\lambda_0-\varepsilon_k)}
 +\frac{2\kappa\varepsilon_k+\varepsilon_k^2}
              {\lambda_0-\varepsilon_k}
 =O(P_k^{-2}).
 \tag{OH.11}
\]

**Proof.** For a real exterior vector `a`, apply (OH.9) to `f=a^TS`. Its exact inner derivative is

\[
 \nabla_z(a^TS)=(-B+W_{zy})a.
\]

Consequently

\[
 a^TC_\nu a
 \le \nu_y\!\left[
 a^T(-B+W_{zy})^T H_I^{-1}(-B+W_{zy})a\right].
 \tag{OH.12}
\]

Write `E=W_zy`. Resolvent comparison and (OH.5) give

\[
 \|H_I^{-1}\|\le(\lambda_0-\varepsilon_k)^{-1},
 \qquad
 \|H_I^{-1}-A^{-1}\|
 \le\frac{\varepsilon_k}{\lambda_0(\lambda_0-\varepsilon_k)}.
 \tag{OH.13}
\]

Expand the expression in (OH.12) around `B^TA^{-1}B`. Its first difference is `B^T(H_I^{-1}-A^{-1})B`. The two cross terms are bounded in absolute quadratic form by `2 kappa epsilon_k/(lambda_0-epsilon_k)`, and the final `E^TH_I^{-1}E` term by `epsilon_k^2/(lambda_0-epsilon_k)`. Their sum is (OH.11), pointwise in `z`. Averaging preserves the inequality. Nonnegativity is the covariance identity itself. ∎

**This is a one-sided Loewner bound.** It is not the assertion `||C_nu-B^TA^{-1}B||=O(P_k^{-2})`. A convex cutoff can reduce a Gaussian covariance by order one. No lower Gaussian comparison is used or needed.

At `W_zz=W_zy=0`, the error vanishes and (OH.10) retains the precise Gaussian Schur contribution even on the literal truncated domain, at every retained exterior force. The mean need not be small. This feature avoids paying a spurious `P_k` factor in the normalizer covariance.

## 4. Its absolute spatial majorant is also uniform

Let `A^IO_{ia}` be the fixed mixed derivative envelope in C8Y.1/RC.4 and put

\[
 C_{ia}=\|B_{ia}\|+A^{IO}_{ia},\qquad
 G_{ij}=\frac2{\lambda_0}e^{-\gamma\rho(i,j)}.
 \tag{OH.14}
\]

For unit scalar directions in exterior blocks `a,b`, C08's covariance inequality applied to the two scores gives

\[
 \|(C_\nu)_{ab}\|_{\rm op}
 \le (C^TGC)_{ab}.
 \tag{OH.15}
\]

Indeed `||D_{z_i}S_a|| <= C_{ia}` pointwise; insert those deterministic bounds in C8A.12 and take the supremum over the two unit directions. For any fixed rate `beta` below the available rates, the triangle inequality yields

\[
 \|C^TGC\|_\beta
 \le\|C^T\|_\beta\|G\|_\beta\|C\|_\beta<\infty.
 \tag{OH.16}
\]

Both row and column sums are retained. Thus the covariance part of the induced outer Hessian is exponentially localized, with constants independent of volume, cutoff depth and history wherever the displayed C08 and mixed-score input bounds hold uniformly. This is a proved consequence of those inequalities, not an independent certification of their all-history application. Unlike the error in the Loewner upper bound, its full absolute norm is generally order one, because it contains the principal cross precision `B`.

## 5. The exact remaining outer curvature and support test

On a smooth positive stratum of (OH.4), differentiation of the same normalizer gives

\[
 D_y^2\log Z(y)=\nu_y W_{yy}+C_\nu(y).
 \tag{OH.17}
\]

No derivative of `B` or `A` occurs because this is the same-current variation at fixed coarse datum. For older native/physical directions those derivatives must be restored, as in RC.19–RC.22.

The outer smooth potential is

\[
 \overline V(y)=\tfrac12y^TD_0y-\log q(y)-\log Z(y).
\]

Define the remaining defect

\[
 \mathcal R(y)=D_y^2\log q(y)+\nu_y W_{yy}(z,y).
 \tag{OH.18}
\]

Then the exact identity and proved bound are

\[
 \begin{split}
 \overline V''(y)&=D_0-\mathcal R(y)-C_\nu(y),\\
 \overline V''(y)&\succeq
 \underbrace{D_0-B^TA^{-1}B}_{\Sigma}
       -\mathcal R(y)-\delta_kI.
 \end{split}
 \tag{OH.19}
\]

The defect is invariant under shifting a scalar `c(y)` from the outer factor into the inner exponent: `W -> W+c`, `q -> q exp(-c)` leaves (OH.18) unchanged. Thus the missing estimate cannot be removed by reallocating a current-independent-in-`z` scalar.

If the full principal matrix in (OH.2) satisfies the source gap `mathcal K >= lambda_0 I`, then

\[
 \Sigma\succeq\lambda_0I.
 \tag{OH.20}
\]

To see this, minimize `(x,a)^T mathcal K (x,a)` over `x`. Its minimum is `a^T Sigma a`, and the full lower bound gives at least `lambda_0 |a|^2`. This keeps the actual principal inverse and all cross coefficients together.

### Corollary OH.3 — sufficient fixed-current outer application

Suppose, additionally, that the actual outer law on this fixed chart has:

1. a fixed convex product support (or a separately proved replacement support theorem whose nonnegative boundary form also admits the same spatial weighted-conjugation estimate);
2. the smooth defect bound `mathcal R <= lambda_0 I/4`;
3. an exponentially summable deterministic entrywise majorant for `mathcal R`, uniformly on that support.

After lowering the common coupling ceiling so that `delta_k <= lambda_0/4`,

\[
 \overline V''\succeq\tfrac12\lambda_0I.
 \tag{OH.21}
\]

The weighted-conjugation and scalar Neumann arguments of C06/C08 then give a fixed exponentially localized covariance kernel for this outer law. The entries of `D_0`, of `C_nu` by (OH.15), and of the stipulated defect are exponentially summable; conjugation at a sufficiently small fixed rate preserves a positive form gap. A product support keeps its boundary form local to the individual coordinate blocks. Nonnegative curvature alone on a general convex nonproduct support would prove a variance bound, but would not justify this spatial conclusion: a global convex constraint can create nonlocal boundary couplings. This proves the stated conditional implication with its stated support hypothesis.

The corollary is not an application to the full history law. C05 controls its identified analytic activity families in their admitted current/native domains, and the conditional-law derivation preserves current-independent native scalars. Those facts do not prove Items 1–3 for all factors and strata in (OH.4). In particular:

- retained current `R`-bad tests can restrict `y` to complements of cutoff balls and more general selected sets;
- changing a mask or a determining component changes the domain/coordinate problem and is not a derivative in the fixed `(z,y)` chart;
- the exterior relocation Jacobian cancels only from the inner normalized ratio, not from `q`;
- an old history mass kept as a fixed parameter by C05 becomes a live factor when the corresponding history is subsequently averaged.

The native derivative bound for an assigned scalar does not supply the missing global selected-support theorem. On open strata an indicator can be constant, while its boundary flux remains essential to covariance estimates.

## 6. Why a positive smooth Hessian is insufficient on the outer bad sectors

### Proposition OH.4 — an elementary selected-domain obstruction

Let `Y` be a standard Gaussian vector in `R^d`, conditioned on `|Y| >= P`. The smooth potential has Hessian exactly `I`, and the conditional mean is zero. Nevertheless

\[
 \operatorname{Var}(Y_1\mid |Y|\ge P)
 =\frac1d\mathbb E[|Y|^2\mid |Y|\ge P]
 \ge\frac{P^2}{d}.
 \tag{OH.22}
\]

**Proof.** Reflection symmetry gives zero mean. Rotational symmetry gives equal second moments whose sum is the radial second moment. The event gives the lower bound. ∎

Thus no cutoff-independent Poincare/covariance constant follows from the local Hessian `I` on that nonconvex selected support. This example is not a counterexample to the Wilson theorem; it demonstrates precisely why the `R`-bad support cannot be ignored when trying to extend the inner C07 argument to the outer variables. Its small probability can be useful in the full law, but that probability and the actual insertion costs must be estimated together. This is the type of H02/H04 sector payment the conditional theorem does not perform.

### Proposition OH.5 — even perfectly local conditional response does not control the outer mixture

Let a finite lattice have variables `z_i` in a fixed symmetric interval `[-P,P]`, with `P>2`, and define

\[
 \nu_y(dz)=\prod_i
 \frac{\mathbf1_{[-P,P]}(z_i)e^{-z_i^2/2+y_i z_i}\,dz_i}
      {\int_{-P}^{P}e^{-u^2/2+y_i u}\,du}.
 \tag{OH.23}
\]

Its conditional Hessian is `I`, its support is a convex product, its off-diagonal conditional covariance is zero, and its response to `y_i` is exactly local. Take the outer law to put probability one half on each configuration `y_i=+1` for every `i` and `y_i=-1` for every `i`. If `m(P)>0` denotes the one-site mean at `y_i=1`, then for distinct sites

\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_{\pi\nu}(z_i,z_j)=m(P)^2,
 \tag{OH.24}
\]

independent of their separation.

**Proof.** Odd symmetry gives the means `+m(P)` and `-m(P)`. Positivity follows because the numerator of the mean is the integral over `u>0` of `u e^{-u^2/2}(e^u-e^{-u})`, which is positive. The conditional off-diagonal covariance is zero, so total covariance is the covariance of the conditional means. ∎

Again this is a logical counterexample to an inference from conditional estimates alone, not a Wilson counterexample. It shows why an estimate for the actual outer law is necessary in the composition kernel `G + T G_out T^T` of RC.26.

## 7. Three M04 distinctions required in the existence route

The M04 analysis contains three relevant distinctions.

First, [First ordinary step: an active geometry pair and a strong-carrier lower bound](../observable_transport/A_support_and_normalization/M04_First_Step_Geometry_Obstruction.md) gives two active admitted first-step histories with the same nearby numerical data and a changed integration domain controlled by distant selector data. Under the original defining-footprint rule, the transported scalar has a nonzero local gap but every distinguishing carrier pays the distant footprint. The resulting lower bound grows like

\[
 \frac{e^{c\kappa M R_1}}{1+P^2},
 \tag{OH.25}
\]

and exceeds the microscopic incoming budget. This is an obstruction to the original full-footprint interface, not as an unproved estimate expected to become true by another C08 application.

Second, [An explicit local-mask interface for the actual positive RG law](../observable_transport/A_support_and_normalization/M04_Local_Mask_Interface.md) introduces independent ambient current masks and a full padded retained regulator. On supported states the mask is still determined by the actual source geometry. The supported laws, marked integrals and finite source jets agree exactly with the old construction, LM.5–LM.9. Passive selection while retaining the old raw state has zero new mark current, LM.10–LM.12. After elimination, however, the actual mask current is the complete normalized difference LM.14–LM.15. A local mask representation does not itself bound that difference or make old global component data local.

Third, [Moving ancestor bases, fixed innovations, and exact latent-gauge current transport](../observable_transport/D_native_nonlinear/M04_Moving_Base_Response_and_Latent_Gauge_Current.md) separates a coherent critical-chain derivative from a chronological fixed-innovation derivative. The exact source identity is

\[
 D_W\Xi[\mathfrak d_W\xi]
 =\mathfrak d_{\Xi}\widetilde\xi
   -D_x\Xi[A_{\widetilde\xi}x].
 \tag{OH.26}
\]

Its second term is a physical innovation response and cannot be dropped by passing to a quotient gauge. MB.12 gives a concrete admitted fixed-innovation response without the desired ancestor-distance suppression. A latent change of variables can cancel the complete gauge response, but only with the insertion, density/divergence and Q-boundary terms all retained:

\[
 \begin{split}
 \dot{\mathbb E}_t f_t={}&
 \mathbb E_t[(\partial_t+w_t\!\cdot\nabla)f_t]
 +\operatorname{Cov}_t(f_t,s_t+\delta_{\rho_t}w_t)\\
 &+Z_t^{-1}(\mathcal B_t-\mathcal F_{w,t})
             [\rho_t(f_t-\mathbb E_t f_t)].
 \end{split}
 \tag{OH.27}
\]

The current C08 theorem controls suitable **fixed-support same-current** covariance terms once their actual Sobolev budgets are given. It does not prove the common arbitrary-depth pullback family, the Q-boundary term, the originwise absolute carrier sum, or joint energy–velocity bounds in the amended M04 norm. Three regular layers and their first source jets are meaningful finite-depth progress, but they do not establish the uniform-depth induction.

The resolvent target MB.30–MB.33 illustrates the exact remaining depth issue: on one actual common family, one needs a small transverse error and estimates for the retained innovation forcing and labelled divergence/boundary terms. C08 cannot justify deleting the forcing term in (OH.26).

## Independent check of the companion continuum calculation

The companion [Physical normalization, ultraviolet bounds and source transport](continuum_bounds.md), EC.6–EC.20, was checked independently at the level of its stated C08 and physical-profile premises. Its new estimate has the correct physical and factorial accounting: the `h^{4m}` quadrature cancels the `h^{-4m}` native field factor; sixth-order diagonal flatness supplies `h^6`; the sole absolute physical root sum costs `h^{-4}`; and the anchored divided-tree sum adds factorial power five to the pointwise power two. Fixed source-block offsets are harmless after replacing `tau^6` by `(1+tau)^6`. The remaining fixed polynomial in `m` is absorbed in `C^m`.

Its fixed logarithmic profile `P(h) <= C(1+log(1/h))^b` costs exactly an additional factorial power `b` after absorption into `h^{2-delta}`, for any fixed `0<delta<2`. That profile requires the stated common physical-scale control, including a bounded terminal inverse-coupling interval where the cited AF comparison is used; it is not inferred solely from a weak-coupling upper ceiling. The geometric ultraviolet sum is then valid. A joint Schwartz seminorm with six derivatives and an integrable root weight controls the Taylor step and is dominated by the displayed linear-order seminorm.

The outer-average conclusion is correct for an outer probability supported on the admitted class, but it remains an average of conditional cumulants. The squarefree-source proof of the complete total-cumulance formula in EC.19 has multiplicity one for each set partition. Its other partition terms, as well as actual microscopic transport, remain outside that conditional shell estimate. This section does not promote EC.15 to ER.7.
